question: Which public draft path can create decision-bearing accepted target tokens for the exact pinned Gemma 4 31B instruction target without changing greedy target semantics?

scope.evidence_fidelity: public immutable model/config and runtime source plus an executed synthetic CPU acceptance/KV consumer
claims_excluded: No public drafter was loaded with model weights in this project.
No c32 acceptance length, verifier time, service time, speedup, or quality result was measured.
A registered upstream test is source-backed load intent, not a measured result from this project.
The CPU fixture proves consumer semantics and shape rejection, not draft quality or target-GPU execution.

text_geometry.layer_pattern: five sliding_attention then one full_attention, repeated ten times

target_tokenizer.required_runtime_rule: Tokenize requests with this target tokenizer only. Draft repositories without tokenizers inherit target token IDs; an assistant tokenizer must not replace this artifact.

registered_source_contracts.dflash_exact_model_names: test/registered/spec/test_gemma4_dflash_31b_extra.py binds google/gemma-4-31B-it plus z-lab/gemma-4-31B-it-DFlash, TP2, block 16, Triton target attention, FlashInfer draft attention, GSM8K score floor 0.75, and mean accept-length floor 5.4.
registered_source_contracts.mtp_exact_model_names: test/registered/spec/test_gemma4_mtp_31b_extra.py binds google/gemma-4-31B-it plus google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant, NEXTN alias, five recurrent steps, top-k 1 or 3, draft budget 6 or 12, GSM8K score floor 0.75, and mean accept-length floor 1.5.

candidate_model.tokenizer: No tokenizer is shipped; target tokenizer is mandatory.

shapes.block_ids: [B,16] int64; column 0 is current target bonus and columns 1:16 begin as mask id 4
shapes.draft_next: [B,15] int64 from the target LM head
shapes.draft_tokens: [B,16] int64 = current token plus 15 simultaneous proposals

producer.source_observation: v0.5.15 creates one [B*16] draft forward, then applies the shared target LM head to hidden[:,1:,:]; there is no per-position Python draft-forward loop.

shapes.target_hidden: [B,16,6*5376] logical captured-feature contract before draft projection

verifier.mask: Standard causal mask over the linear block; target checkpoint supplies every decision.

shapes.out_tokens: [B,16] with only the first commit_lens entries valid per row

kv_commit.logical_contract: For accepted count a, target verify-input KV for candidates[0:a+1] is logically committed; candidates[a+1:16] are not part of the sequence. Output emits candidates[1:a+1] then target_top1[a]. The target bonus remains pending for the next decode forward.

shapes.draft_hidden_materialization: [B,16,*] filtered by commit_lens into draft KV

candidate_paths.close_reason: The implemented producer advances through a recurrent Python loop and therefore does not meet the project's one-forward parallel-draft mechanism. Exact target verification could preserve semantics, but acceptance and economics transfer from the base-trained head are unproven.

producer.source_observation: The worker performs one seed assistant forward and then a recurrent assistant forward for every speculative step except the last.

target_semantic_invariants.rule: The verifier is exactly google/gemma-4-31B-it@b9ea41a2887d8607f594846523f94c6cc75ac8a4; no target weights, layer geometry, tokenizer, logits, or sampling parameters may be replaced by the drafter.
All requests and returned IDs use target tokenizer cc8d3a0c...; assistant tokenizer 75a6583c... cannot become the serving tokenizer.
Each accepted proposal must equal the target decision evaluated on the same already-accepted prefix. Linear DFlash uses a causal block; tree producers use their ancestor mask and retrieval indices.
Stop at the first mismatch on a chain. Never accept a later matching token after a rejected ancestor.
Every speculative round emits one target-selected bonus at the first rejected location or after the fully accepted prefix.
Only target KV belonging to the current token plus accepted draft path becomes logically committed. All rejected branches/suffix slots are freed or excluded by committed length.
The emitted target bonus has not yet been consumed as a target input; it remains pending for the next forward and must not be falsely treated as materialized KV.
This project's executable oracle covers temperature=0 greedy c32. Non-greedy rejection sampling needs a separate execution-equivalent consumer before a semantics claim.

invalid_attempt.classification: observer serialization mismatch; proposal, target, acceptance, and KV computation unchanged for corrected run

competing_explanations.explanation: The public DFlash repo names google/gemma-4-31B-it but does not bind target revision b9ea41...; identical geometry can load while proposal acceptance collapses.
competing_explanations.discriminator: Load both immutable revisions and report c32 accepted-draft histogram and first-mismatch positions.

competing_explanations.explanation: At c32, a [512,262144] target-logit verification surface plus draft work may cost more than saved autoregressive forwards even with useful acceptance.
competing_explanations.discriminator: CUDA-event union for draft, target verify, acceptance, and KV commit; report accepted target tokens per verifier second and per combined draft+verify second.

competing_explanations.explanation: The v0.5.15 registered DFlash and MTP tests prove maintained source intent and exact model names, not that the pinned revisions load in this campaign environment.
competing_explanations.discriminator: First tiny exact-revision target-GPU call followed immediately by the component run.

competing_explanations.explanation: A runtime can compute correct acceptance while committing a rejected suffix or relaying the wrong target hidden state into the next draft round.
competing_explanations.discriminator: For selected rounds, compare committed sequence positions, target KV slot identities, pending bonus, first next-round logits, and AR control.

competing_explanations.explanation: Campaign outputs may repeat enough that the no-weight NGRAM producer delivers similar accepted work without a 3.07 GB draft model.
competing_explanations.discriminator: Run NGRAM as the same target-verifier control and compare accepted target tokens per verifier second plus combined producer+verifier second.

competing_explanations.explanation: EAGLE-3 or frozen-KV MTP can remain economical despite failing the one-forward mechanism criterion because each small recurrent call is cheap and acceptance is higher.
competing_explanations.discriminator: Outside this project's selected mechanism, compare combined draft+verify target-token throughput only if DFlash fails its component gate.

decision.promotion_scope: one exact target-GPU component and c32 acceptance/economics discriminator; not endpoint or production promotion
decision.reason: DFlash is the only compared public learned path whose current source creates all 15 next-token proposals in one draft forward. Its public config exactly matches target hidden width, vocabulary, and 60-layer tap contract. The executed CPU consumer proves the target-prefix, target-bonus, rejected-suffix, and pending-bonus KV semantics for every block-16 acceptance boundary. Actual exact-revision loading and c32 economics remain unmeasured and are the next gate.

next_target_gpu_component.component_promote_rule: Promote to a matched endpoint only if exact semantics and KV audits pass, mean accepted drafts is positive, DFlash accepted-target-tokens per combined draft+verify second exceeds both AR and NGRAM controls, and the measured margin is large enough to make a 20% endpoint reduction plausible. Record any smaller positive gain as stackable evidence rather than silently discarding it.
next_target_gpu_component.component_close_rule: Close this DFlash revision if immutable exact revisions cannot load for a model/shape reason, target semantics or KV path fails after localized runtime defects are repaired, or combined producer+verifier throughput is no better than both exact controls. Low c32 acceptance closes this checkpoint revision, not parallel drafting generally.
